breakpoints.note: The libFuzzer harness hands the exact staged PHP script buffer to the engine. Source scoring begins later inside `zend_compile_attributes()`, but this is the saved entry from the harness into project code.

First project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled attribute arguments on the vulnerable path. For the staged parameter attribute, this statement produces a `ZEND_AST_ARG_LIST` with two children: a valid first argument (`self::class`) and the invalid dynamic class-constant second argument (`s->getAtelf::FOO`).

The flexible `attr->argv[]` storage is allocated from raw `pemalloc()` memory and vulnerable code does not initialize each slot to `IS_UNDEF` before later population and cleanup. Because the attribute is inserted into the attribute hash before all arguments are compiled, any fatal error during argument compilation leaves trailing `argv[]` slots uninitialized but still subject to destruction. The fix adds a loop that applies `ZVAL_UNDEF(&attr->argv[i])` for every declared argument.
